data.title: bn-1qd: Capture tagged runtime layers and collision context

data.body: [P1] The per-frame reset retains every historical tag key, so the 32-layer bound is consumed across the whole session rather than by the current frame. After 32 distinct tags have appeared (for example across level-specific scenes), any genuinely new tag is dropped forever even if only one old tag draws now; a final capture then fails with capacity overflow. Recycle/remove inactive keys at the frame boundary (while keeping at most 32 buffers if desired) and add a regression that draws 32 tags in one frame, then a new tag alone in the next frame.

[P2] This rejects the empty string even though draw_tag("") is a valid, distinct tag under the existing Lua API (which only enforces the 64-byte maximum), and the new docs say layers map exact draw_tag names. Such a captured layer can therefore never be requested. Either accept the empty key here and test it, or make empty tags invalid consistently in draw_tag and document that API change.

data.reason: Request changes: inactive historical tags permanently consume the 32-layer capacity, and scenario validation cannot request a valid empty draw_tag name. Core rendering equivalence, sentinel alpha, replay/reset, path normalization, and focused tests otherwise look sound.

data.body: Fixed in b0f1d7c: per-frame reset now clears historical keys, and a 40-frame rotating-tag regression proves each new current-frame tag remains capturable with zero drops.
Fixed in b0f1d7c: scenario mappings now accept the exact empty-string tag, retain __untagged__ as the distinct None sentinel, and integration coverage captures both in one frame.

data.reason: Approved at b0f1d7c: the cap is now current-frame scoped, the rotating-tag regression catches the prior lifetime exhaustion, and exact empty-string tags remain distinct from __untagged__ with integration coverage. Focused core and playtest tests pass.
